extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent practitioners, and parties seeking or defending post-grant proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and procedural standards for inventor oaths/declarations, filing by non-inventors, specification/claim form rules, the prior-commercial-use defense, and inter partes (post-grant) review procedures under the America Invents Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual who is the inventor or a joint inventor of a claimed invention in an application for patent shall execute an oath or declaration in connection with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath/declaration is required from each inventor unless otherwise provided. (Section text establishes this as a mandatory filing condition.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements in oath or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration shall contain statements that (1) the application was made or was authorized to be made by the affiant or declarant; and (2) such individual believes himself or herself to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two explicit statements must appear in the inventor's oath/declaration; Director may specify additional required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may require additional information in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may specify additional information relating to the inventor and the invention that is required to be included in an oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations may expand what must be included beyond the statutory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement permitted (in lieu of oath/declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of executing an oath or declaration, the applicant may provide a substitute statement under permitted circumstances specified in statute and by Director regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute statement is available only under defined circumstances (see next entries); Director may add further permitted circumstances by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted bases for substitute statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement is permitted if the individual is (A) unable to file the oath/declaration because (i) deceased, (ii) under legal incapacity, or (iii) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort; or (B) is under an obligation to assign but has refused to make the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit statutory bases permitting a substitute statement; Director may permit additional circumstances by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of substitute statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement must (A) identify the individual with respect to whom the statement applies; (B) set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis for filing the substitute statement in lieu of the oath/declaration; and (C) contain any additional information, including any showing, required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements must explain why the oath cannot be filed and include any Director-required showings or information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements may be included in assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual under an obligation of assignment may include the required statements in the assignment executed by the individual, in lieu of filing such statements separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording an assignment with the required statements can satisfy oath/declaration/substitute statement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing oaths/declarations or substitute statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of allowance may be provided to an applicant only if the applicant has filed each required oath or declaration or has filed a substitute statement or recorded an assignment meeting the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of required statements is a condition precedent to receiving a notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier-filed application exception (retained statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements do not apply if an earlier-filed application to which the later application claims benefit contains an executed oath/declaration, substitute statement, or assignment that meets the requirements, subject to Director's ability to require copies be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant relying on earlier filings may nonetheless be required by the Director to include copies of those documents in the later application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; filing additional statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a required statement may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time; the Director shall establish regulations for filing additional statements if inventor naming changes. Once a compliant oath/declaration or assignment is filed, the Director may not require that individual to make additional equivalent statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements can be corrected or supplemented; failure to comply that is remedied will not render a patent invalid or unenforceable (savings clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of penalties in declarations/statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed pursuant to this section shall contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. §1001 by fine or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute requires an express acknowledgment of criminal penalties for willful false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by person other than inventor (§118) — who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention may make an application for patent. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest may make an application on behalf of and as agent for the inventor on proof of pertinent facts and that such action is appropriate to preserve rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director grants a patent on such an application, the patent is granted to the real party in interest with notice to the inventor as the Director considers sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification requirements (35 U.S.C. 112 — written description/enablement framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using it, and enablement (as recast by amended subsection headings: e.g., ‘(a) IN GENERAL.—The specification…’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory text restructures section 112 into labeled subsections (a)–(f); language revisions emphasize inventor/joint inventor perspective in the enablement/written description phrasing and reorganize claim/claim-form rules (form; dependent references; multiple dependent claims; elements in combination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense to infringement based on prior commercial use — substantive entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is entitled to a defense under section 282(b) with respect to subject matter (process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter used in a commercial process) that would otherwise infringe, if (1) such person, acting in good faith, commercially used the subject matter in the United States (internal commercial use or an arm’s length sale/transfer of a useful end result), and (2) such commercial use occurred at least 1 year before the earlier of (A) the effective filing date of the claimed invention or (B) the date the claimed invention was publicly disclosed in a manner qualifying for the exception under section 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defense applies only to qualifying commercial uses in the US and is time-limited to uses at least one year prior to the earlier of filing date or qualifying public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for prior commercial use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: A person asserting this defense shall have the burden of establishing the defense by clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute places a heightened evidentiary burden on the party asserting the prior commercial use defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional commercial uses counted — premarketing regulatory review
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter subject to a premarketing regulatory review period during which safety or efficacy is established (including periods specified in §156(g)) shall be deemed commercially used for purposes of the defense during such regulatory review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory periods that precede commercial marketing may nonetheless qualify as 'commercial use' for the defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional commercial uses counted — nonprofit laboratory use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use by a nonprofit research laboratory or other nonprofit entity (e.g., university or hospital) for which the public is the intended beneficiary shall be deemed to be a commercial use for purposes of the defense, except that the defense may be asserted pursuant to this paragraph only for continued and noncommercial use by and in the laboratory or other nonprofit entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprofit research uses can qualify but are narrowly limited to continued/noncommercial in-lab use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rights when defense-holder sells useful end result
rubrics_metrics.description: The sale or other disposition of a useful end result by a person entitled to assert the defense shall exhaust the patent owner’s rights under the patent to the extent such rights would have been exhausted had the sale been made by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defense-holder’s disposition can create exhaustion comparable to that arising from a patent owner’s sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal defense limitation and transfer restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The defense may be asserted only by the person who performed or directed the commercial use, or by an entity that controls/is controlled by/under common control with such person. Except for transfers to the patent owner, the right to assert the defense may not be licensed/assigned/transferred except as an ancillary/subordinate part of a good-faith assignment/transfer of the entire enterprise or line of business to which the defense relates. If acquired as part of an assignment/transfer, the defense may be asserted only for uses at sites where the subject matter was in use before the later of the effective filing date or the date of assignment/transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The defense is personal to the user and is narrowly alienable; site restrictions apply on transferred defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation bar to assertion of prior commercial use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not assert the defense if the subject matter on which the defense is based was derived from the patentee or persons in privity with the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant must show independent commercial development; derivation from patentee precludes the defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense is not a general license — scope limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The defense is not a general license under all claims of the patent; it extends only to the specific subject matter for which a qualifying commercial use has been established, but includes variations in quantity/volume and improvements that do not infringe additional specifically claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of protection is narrowly tailored to the particular subject matter and uses proven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of use bars reliance going forward
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who abandoned commercial use that would have qualified may not rely on activities performed before abandonment to establish the defense with respect to actions taken on or after the date of such abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity of use matters; abandonment defeats later assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: University exception to prior commercial use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: A person commercially using subject matter may not assert the defense if the claimed invention was, at the time made, owned by or subject to an obligation to assign to an institution of higher education or a technology transfer organization whose primary purpose is commercialization, except where the activities required to reduce to practice could not have been undertaken using federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute preserves universities' ownership/assignment obligations from being undermined by this defense, with a limited exception tied to federal funding constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for unreasonable assertion of defense
rubrics_metrics.description: If the defense is pleaded by an infringer who is found to infringe and subsequently fails to demonstrate a reasonable basis for asserting the defense, the court shall find the case exceptional for awarding attorney fees under §285.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreasonable reliance on the defense can expose the asserting party to fee shifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity unaffected by assertion of prior commercial use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be deemed invalid under §§102 or 103 solely because a defense is raised or established under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing the defense does not by itself render the patent invalid as prior art under statutory novelty/obviousness provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes review — who may petition and fee authority (§311)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file with the Office a petition to institute an inter partes review of the patent. The Director shall establish, by regulation, fees to be paid by the person requesting the review, in amounts the Director determines reasonable considering aggregate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute authorizes third parties (non-owners) to seek IPR and charges the Director with fee-setting authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inter partes review (§311(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may request cancellation of one or more claims only on a ground that could be raised under §§102 or 103 and only on the basis of prior art consisting of patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR is limited to patentability challenges based on patents/printed publications under novelty/obviousness grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for inter partes review (§311(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for IPR shall be filed after the later of either (1) the date 9 months after grant of a patent or issuance of a reissue, or (2) if a post-grant review is instituted, the date of termination of such post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets a statutory window tied to patent grant and overlapping post-grant review proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content requirements (§312(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be considered only if: (1) accompanied by payment of fee; (2) identifies all real parties in interest; (3) identifies in writing and with particularity each claim challenged, the grounds for challenge to each claim, and the evidence supporting the grounds, including (A) copies of patents/printed publications relied upon and (B) affidavits/declarations if relying on expert opinions; (4) provides other information as the Director may require; and (5) provides copies of required documents to the patent owner or designated representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be detailed and documentary; service on patent owner required; Director may require additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petitions (§312(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after receipt of a petition, the Director shall make the petition available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR petition filings are publicly posted unless sealed per regulation/motion to seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner's right to preliminary response (§313)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IPR petition is filed, the patent owner has the right to file a preliminary response within a time set by the Director, setting forth reasons why no IPR should be instituted based upon the petition's failure to meet any requirement of the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners can challenge sufficiency of petitions before institution determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution threshold for IPR (§314(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize IPR to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information in the petition and any response shows there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one of the claims challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute establishes a 'reasonable likelihood' threshold for institution (lower than ultimate proof standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for institution decision (§314(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall determine whether to institute IPR within 3 months after receiving a preliminary response or, if none filed, the last date on which such response may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution determination is time-limited to promote prompt resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and finality of institution decision (§314(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall notify petitioner and patent owner in writing of the determination and make it public, including the date review commences. The Director's determination whether to institute IPR is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution is publicly announced and not subject to immediate appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to civil actions — bars and stays (§315(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR may not be instituted if, before the petition is filed, the petitioner or real party filed a civil action challenging validity. If a civil action challenging validity is filed on or after a petition, that civil action is automatically stayed until specified events. A counterclaim challenging validity does not constitute a civil action for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute coordinates IPR with district court litigation via institution bars and automatic stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year bar after service of infringement complaint (§315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR may not be instituted if the petition is filed more than 1 year after the date on which the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy was served with a complaint alleging infringement, except that the time limitation does not apply to a request for joinder under §315(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of an infringement complaint triggers a one-year filing bar for IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder discretion (§315(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director institutes IPR, the Director may, in discretion, join as a party any person who properly files a petition determined to warrant institution after preliminary response or response period expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may add additional petitioners into an instituted IPR at his/her discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from IPR (§315(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner (or its real party in interest/privy) in an IPR that results in a final written decision may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground raised or reasonably could have been raised during that IPR; likewise, may not assert in certain civil actions or ITC proceedings that the claim is invalid on any ground raised or reasonably could have been raised during that IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution and final written decision create statutory estoppel against re-litigating grounds that were or could have been raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations governing conduct of IPR (§316(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall prescribe regulations providing (inter alia) public availability of files, standards for showing sufficient grounds to institute, procedures for submission of supplemental information, discovery standards limited to depositions of declarants and what is necessary in interest of justice, sanctions for abuse, protective orders, requirement that patent owner be allowed to file a response with affidavits/declarations, standards/procedures for motions to amend, oral hearing rights, and timing rules for final determination (1 year with up to 6-month extension for good cause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute directs broad regulatory framework including limits on discovery, public access, amendment procedure, hearing rights, sanctions, and strict time limits subject to limited extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's considerations in prescribing regulations (§316(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations, Director shall consider effect on the economy, integrity of the patent system, efficient administration of the Office, and ability of the Office to timely complete proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design must balance administrative efficiency, system integrity, and economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board to conduct IPRs (§316(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall conduct each IPR instituted under this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB is the statutorily-designated tribunal for IPR proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the patent during IPR (§316(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: During an instituted IPR, the patent owner may file one motion to amend to (A) cancel any challenged patent claim, and/or (B) for each challenged claim propose a reasonable number of substitute claims. Additional motions may be permitted jointly to materially advance settlement or as permitted by regulation. An amendment may not enlarge the scope of claims or introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner is given a narrow, regulated opportunity to amend claims; amendments cannot broaden claim scope or add new matter; information submitted in support of amendments becomes public prosecution history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards in IPR (§316(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an IPR instituted under this chapter, the petitioner has the burden of proving unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must meet preponderance standard at trial-phase, distinct from the clear-and-convincing burden in district court invalidity defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement procedures for IPR (§317)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IPR shall be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon the joint request of the petitioner and patent owner unless the Office has decided the merits. If terminated with respect to a petitioner, no estoppel under §315(e) shall attach to that petitioner. Any agreement made in connection with termination must be in writing and filed in the Office before termination; may be treated as business confidential on showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement is possible but subject to filing and disclosure requirements; termination before merits avoids estoppel for that petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and certificate (§318)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IPR is instituted and not dismissed, the PTAB shall issue a final written decision on patentability of any challenged claim and any new claim added under §316(d). Where final decision issued and appeals exhausted/terminated, Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming any claim determined patentable, and incorporating any new/amended claim determined patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final PTAB decisions are implemented by official certificates that alter patent claims and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended/new claims (§318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following IPR shall have the same effect as specified in §252 for reissued patents regarding the rights of persons who made/purchased/used or imported the subject matter or prepared substantially therefor before issuance of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments can create intervening rights protecting earlier users from certain infringement claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public data on length of review (§318(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make available to the public data describing the length of time between institution and issuance of a final written decision for each IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement to publish statistics on IPR durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal final PTAB decision (§319)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the final written decision of the PTAB may appeal pursuant to §§141–144; any party to the IPR has the right to be a party to the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute preserves appellate rights from PTAB to the designated appellate venue under the patent statutes.
